title: DR1's declaration makes the user accountable for destruction and disposal costs only when the authorities instruct it; the frontend's version of the same list drops that condition and the word "any" from all four items.

controls.text: I confirm that I am accountable for:

finding.frontend: The four bullets under "I confirm that I am accountable for:" read "payments for border control checks", "re-dispatch of the consignment", "quarantine or isolation of the animals" and "the costs of destruction and disposal" (`src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/declaration/copy/copy.en.js:8-13`). The last one is unconditional: the user agrees to the costs of destruction and disposal with no statement of who decides that destruction happens.
finding.prototype: DR1's four read "any payment for the official controls at the border", "any arrangements to re-dispatch the consignment", "any costs needed for quarantine or isolation of consignments" and "any costs needed for destruction and disposal of consignments, when instructed by the authorities" (`app/views/declaration.html:57-60`). Two differences carry weight rather than being tidying: DR1 opens each item with "any", which scopes the commitment, and it makes the fourth conditional on an instruction from the authorities, which narrows what the user is agreeing to.
finding.difference: Replace the four strings in the declaration copy with DR1's. No template change is needed — the list already renders from an array — and the Welsh strings need the same treatment. Legal text: take DR1's wording unchanged, in particular the "when instructed by the authorities" qualifier, because dropping it widens the user's liability rather than shortening a sentence.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding the phrase "when instructed by the authorities" in the frontend's declaration bullets.
finding.verification: Read both declaration DOMs, opened both full-page shots, and read copy.en.js:8-13 and declaration.html:57-60 at the cited lines. The frontend DOM carries the four bullets exactly as quoted and the prototype DOM carries DR1's four exactly as quoted, including the "when instructed by the authorities" tail. Ran the falsifier: `grep -c 'when instructed by the authorities'` against fe-declaration.html returns 0, so it does not fire. Both citations resolve to what the sentence says. CORRECT.

relatedTo.why: Both are clauses of the same declaration and both need the same legal sign-off before the copy changes.
